model_annotations.Bulgarian: Figure 5 is a bar graph that compares per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, ranging from 10% to 80%, with increments of 10%. The vertical axis represents perplexity on a logarithmic scale, spanning from 10^1 to 10^3. Two types of bars are present: blue bars representing "Per-Output" and orange bars representing "Per- Layer". The graph shows that as the sparsity rate increases, the perplexity of both Per-Output and Per-Layer increases. At lower sparsity rates (10%-40%), the perplexity values for Per-Output and Per-Layer are relatively close, with Per-Output values slightly lower than or nearly equal to Per-Layer values. At higher sparsity rates (50%-80%), the perplexity values for Per-Layer exceed those of Per-Output, with the difference becoming more pronounced at 70% and 80% sparsity rates. Representative perplexity values include approximately 5.70 for Per-Output and 5.70 for Per-Layer at 10% sparsity, and around 534.42 for Per-Output and 886.10 for Per-Layer at 80% sparsity.
model_annotations.Chinese:
This figure presents a comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, with labels at 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, and appears to be linear. The vertical axis, labeled "Perplexity", is on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^1 to 10^3. 

The figure features two groups of bars: blue bars representing "Per-Output" perplexity and orange bars representing "Per-Layer" perplexity. At 10% sparsity, both types of perplexity are approximately 5.7. As sparsity increases, perplexity generally increases for both types. Notably, at lower sparsity rates (up to around 50%), the blue and orange bars are of similar heights, with values ranging from about 5.7 to 7.7. At higher sparsity rates (70% and 80%), the orange bars are significantly taller than the blue bars, with values reaching around 886 for "Per-Layer" perplexity at 80% sparsity, compared to about 534 for "Per-Output" perplexity. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or other means. The bars are not sorted in any specific order beyond the increasing sparsity rate along the horizontal axis.
